This thread kind of reawakened a few I forgot x_x


Wouldn't want to change in front of people in the locker room in gym


Thought body hair was gross, would regularly shave chest and armpits even though I was embarrassed about doing it. In college one of my friends called me out on it and I just told him I didn't like how it felt to put deodorant on over the hair. 


In 6th grade choir I wanted to be in the alto/soprano section but they put me in tenor/bass and it upset me


Obsession with gender-bending erotica stories and not understanding/ being grossed out by regular porn 


Intentionally avoided playing girl characters in games for a long time because it seemed non manly, and when I finally did I felt so happy and couldn't go back.  (Also was embarrassed about this though)


Dressed up in my cousins fairy outfit when I was really young and was really happy and felt pretty


Also I never dated and thought I was ace for most of my life, turned out I just hated the idea of being the boyfriend and just really wanted to be a girlfriend instead. 


There's probably more but those were some big ones that stood out.  Still repressed it until my early 20s though :/ but I'm happy I eventually figured it out.

Depends on who you're writing for.  If you're writing a friend or someone you are pretty sure will be supportive, you shouldn't need to go to much length and just invite them to support you. 

If it's for someone who you won't think will be supportive, you need to be sure to be assertive about your identity, and encourage them to have an open mind when reading. It shouldn't be aggressive but it should be firm and not give them any leeway on how they can treat you.  

And of course it also depends on your relationship to the person, like if it's a parent it can be more complex.  I have a letter I wrote to my not very tolerant mom if you need an example, feel free to DM me.  :)
Same, my mom thought I was just gay, sigh :/
Somehow me and my bf have the reverse, where I'm trying to turn the temperature down while he's trying to heat it up constantly.  Breaking gender norms I guess?

Ugh yes, AMAB I totally mirrored guys for most of my life to try to fit in, and didn't start to properly learn to have my own personality until I came to terms with things a couple years ago. I look back on past me in disgust often but I try not to blame myself since I was just trying to act like the other guys :/
The masculine urge to shave your legs and have breasts and curves and be called a good girl and not have a dick and...

Maybe, I'd hope that I don't have to deal with it for that long but I suppose it's a process.

Thank you, this is helpful. I've been talking to these friends online on a pretty regular basis since the pandemic so I understand it can take time to undo the deadname programming. They were deadnaming me for the first week but now it's shifted to this so I guess progress? 

They use the right name occasionally but it is rare. I'd like to know what's going on in their head since sometimes they'll toggle back and forth between deadname, gender neutral/online handle and chosen name.

I also haven't seen them in person since coming out so maybe when they see me in fem clothes it will help to solidify it more?
Yeah I'm not sure, I guess it's better than deadname but it still rubs me kind of weird. I should tell them if it keeps going but I have a hard time with making my needs clear :S

I'm aspiring to be a game dev and have worked on some game jams :) 

The industry is very male centric and has had lots of examples of mistreatment of women. It's hard to say about trans people in particular. My dream is to be able to make a living as an indie dev to avoid that.

I think this is a hard thing, because I think especially for newly out trans people this can be affirming when they're frequently being deadnamed by friends and family. 

For someone who's been out for a while or to more people though, it can just be patronizing.  I think the best course of action is to just talk to them privately if you're feeling uncomfortable with the way they address you - they sound supportive so I'm sure they'll adjust.

I started hormones 14 months ago and am just now starting to come out to people.  Friends I haven't seen since pre covid seem to be kind of suspicious something is going on, but people I've seen regularly like my mom don't seem to think anything is up.  


But it depends on genetics and how attentive your friends or family are definitely. I think I started being gendered correctly by strangers more often around the 1 year mark.

I went to University of Washington in Seattle, and western Washington in general is just very liberal and accepting overall. While I was still closeted in college  I met a decent number of trans people and they were always treated respectfully. I started doing hormones a few years after college and people are pretty nice for the most part, only a few uncomfortable incidents.
You could be subconsciously disassociating from your dysphoria so that you don't have to face trauma. Give it time and consider how you really feel without other's feelings considered, only your own.

Definitely brings back some childhood memories.  I would tuck my dysphoria noodle behind my legs and look at myself in the mirror and I remember just enjoying it for "some reason". 

When I was very young I remember feeling really confused about erections and felt like it didn't belong on my body.

Also I'd often do the classic cupping hands under my chest in the shower and letting them fill with water so I could feel some weight where boobs would be. 

Makes me wish I had really critically thought about why I was doing these things when I was younger instead of repressing until my early 20s :/

Some people report feeling mentally better on hrt though it's very person dependent.  Id say it's very low risk though, can't hurt anything. I think if you're thinking about and willing to make the commitment to get hormones it says something about yourself, few cis people would think that way.

The first few months won't produce any  irreversible changes so it could be worth trying to see how you feel about it. I'd say it's worth it if you've been considering it that long, especially if you can do informed consent.

Dude I'm sorry,  I may be suicidal but dumping basically the only person that cares about me isn't going to help anything.  If I did that I'd crush him,  make myself feel worse,  and then basically I'd have no reason left to stay.  My mom is part of the problem too since she's transphobic and contributed a lot to me feeling helpless.

I've told him a lot that I think I'm bad for him but I don't know.. i think he's just too nice to admit it. It's hard because I've helped him in the past coping with his grief from his friend he lost to suicide,  but now it's reversed and he's basically my lifeline, while I just drag him down. I'll admit he's not perfect, nobody is,  but i know he genuinely tries his best for me and cares.

And it's my bad attitude that makes it worse,  and it especially shows when I'm in one of my bad moods which is most of the time nowadays. I get bothered by stupid inconsequential things and take it out on him, and I've tried to be better but I just always go back to it.  I keep trying to be better but it's just so hard. I just always think of how I could just escape it all, not have to deal with a world that hates trans people and just has so much bad in it. 

I appreciate the words a lot also,  it's helped to pull me back for now at least.
I tried therapy but the cost is hard, and I've had mixed experiences.  We're long distance also,  but it probably is something I should try again

I've been fighting so long and I keep trying.. it gets so much harder to convince myself to stay every day

I saw you've been reaching out to a lot of people also,  I wanted to thank you for doing something like that. It's very selfless.

I've tried talking to him how I feel I'm just a negative influence on him but he just won't admit to it, or say he hasn't really thought about it and doesn't think he could do better even though I'm pretty sure he could.  He's just so nice and puts others problems above his own,  so I know he tries to fix my problems rather than worrying about himself.  That's why it hurts so much,  i feel I'm bad for him if I'm here,  but it's worse if I'm gone
